A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 92-model study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The original figures and appendix material can be matched across the revision and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-validated performance-prediction results, fitted scaling relationships, and feature-importance analyses, including Table 2 and the appendix SHAP plots.

after.justification: v2 retains original analyses and adds human annotation results, training-corpus correlation analyses, and controlled pretraining experiments with 460M-parameter models.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains documentation-derived and free-generation features, GPT-4o-mini domain classification, greedy feature selection, XGBoost prediction, and SHAP analysis. The added validations and comparison methods do not establish a revision to this procedure.

E1.justification: The 92-model database and twelve downstream benchmark families remain unchanged. Appendices F and G add direct document-label and corpus-reconstruction validation using the Pile, SmolLM corpus, and RefinedWeb. The controlled Dolma experiments reuse existing language, code, mathematics, and factuality task domains.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Table 2 add an evaluated log-linear predictor based on parameter and token counts alongside the existing median and scale-only XGBoost baselines. LightGBM was already reported as tested in v1; v2 supplies its numerical results in Table 9.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled 460M-parameter pretraining with fixed hyperparameters, 10B training tokens, and a cosine schedule spanning 100B tokens. It tests 10/20/25/30% code and 30/50/90% web mixtures using answer-loss and TruthfulQA margin metrics. New validation protocols include annotation filtering and sampled-corpus comparisons. The original nested three-fold predictor evaluation is retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's SHAP analyses, generation examples, and qualitative classifier check, v2 adds quantitative human validation of domain classification, comparisons between free-generations and actual training corpora, and controlled data-mixture ablations. These test both measurement reliability and whether observational predictions survive controlled pretraining experiments.

E5.justification: The original 50-seed predictor comparisons, 95% confidence intervals, paired t-tests, and false-discovery-rate correction remain. v2 adds correlation p-values and Cohen's kappa for validation. Table 9 newly specifies one LightGBM run without significance testing, and Appendix M discloses seed 42 without reporting repeated-seed uncertainty for the pretraining experiments.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains the accuracy-task MAEs but revises scaled Brier MAEs: XNLI scaling/all-features values change from 6.68/6.30 to 5.11/4.30, and ANLI from 6.74/6.53 to 6.18/5.86. Some baselines and p-values also change. New results include 85.8% classifier agreement, corpus-feature correlations, LightGBM scores, and controlled mixture losses. Table 11 reports declining TruthfulQA accuracy with more web data, but the lowest margin loss occurs at 50% web.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the Brier-score definition by squaring the residual and making the summation index consistent with k. This changes the mathematical expression, without establishing that the implementation or experiments changed. The scaling-law and predictor formulations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces its highlighted claim about rotary versus learned embeddings with the negative impact of web data on truthfulness. The central 92-model analysis, reported 3–28% predictive-error reduction, and 15–25% code/language trade-off remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new correlations as supporting free-generation proxies while distinguishing stronger domain fidelity from weaker stylistic fidelity. Section 6 argues that controlled runs provide preliminary support for predicting training decisions, introduces an approximately 8% code optimum for language-only performance, and acknowledges the nonmonotonic TruthfulQA margin loss. The dedicated limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix M adds the training library, architecture configuration, hyperparameters, Dolma-v1 mixture construction, evaluation masking and normalization, eight-H100 hardware setup, and approximately six-hour checkpoint training time. Appendices F/G document filtering and reservoir sampling. The code/data link changes from GitHub to an anonymous hosting address, and the feature table removes one of two conflicting GSM8K entries.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Although related-work prose is condensed and renumbered, the paper retains its positioning relative to controlled data ablations, observational scaling, data selection, and tracing capabilities to training data.

P1.justification: Several passages in Sections 3, 5.2, and related work are shortened, a confirmatory-experiments section is inserted, and the appendices are extended and renumbered. The overall narrative remains recognizable. The affiliation is corrected, and personal acknowledgments are replaced by an AI-assistance disclosure.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the evidence displays with Figure 6's mixture-performance plots, correlation Tables 6–7, and LightGBM and pretraining-result Tables 9–11. Table 2 gains a log-linear column, and some existing displays are resized or relocated. All original plots are retained; appendix SHAP plots are renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: Quantitative classifier validation, corpus comparisons, and controlled mixture experiments strengthen evidence that v1 supported mainly through observational analysis and qualitative checks. The Brier formula is also corrected. However, the early 460M checkpoints lack repeated-seed uncertainty, and the stated approximately 8% code optimum is outside the tested 10–30% range. Reporting consistency also slips: Section 5.1 retains a 3–6% Brier-error reduction summary although revised XNLI results imply about 16%. The additions provide a useful but limited net improvement.
